reasons: Official cite 496 U.S. 444, parallels 110 S. Ct. 2481 / 110 L. Ed. 2d 412 / 58 U.S.L.W. 4781, and vendor-neutral 1990 U.S. LEXIS 3144 all match the lake citations block exactly.
Cached opinion corroborates identity: Rehnquist, C.J. opinion, sobriety-checkpoint holding, star pages *447-*455, decided 1990.
Frontmatter homes lists [[Checkpoints and Roadblocks]] as 'Key — Anchor', matching the assertion payload.
Sitz is the seminal suspicionless-sobriety-checkpoint decision; anchor role on a checkpoints page is substantively supported by the disclosed opinion.
Opinion holds the sobriety-checkpoint program 'is consistent with the Fourth Amendment' after balancing the State's interest in preventing drunken driving, effectiveness, and intrusion (b497-5).

Holding field ('Suspicionless sobriety (DUI) checkpoints are constitutional; the state's interest in combating drunk driving...') is an accurate paraphrase; trailing ellipsis is normal frontmatter truncation.
field_i_validity good_law (migration-seed) is correct: Sitz remains good law for sobriety checkpoints.

scope_note accurately states Sitz is distinguished by City of Indianapolis v. Edmond for checkpoints whose primary purpose is general crime control; content page's 'distinguished by' framing matches doctrine.
residual_risks: Lake carries many proposed:true negative edges (field_ii questioned/overruled/superseded, e.g. Edmond, Harmelin, Midgette) from lane1_negative/lane2_top_cited; these are unadjudicated citator-noise (several doctrinally implausible) and do not disturb the migration-seed good_law basis.

Opinion at *705 (b750-7): 'we hold that a warrant to search for contraband founded on probable cause implicitly carries with it the limited authority to detain the occupants of the premises while a proper search is conducted.'
Holding field paraphrase ('A warrant to search premises for contraband, founded on probable cause, implicitly carries the limited authority to detain the occupants...') faithfully tracks that text.
Frontmatter homes lists [[Securing the Scene]] with role 'Related (scene-securing overlap)', matching the assertion payload exactly.
Summers (detention of occupants during warrant execution) substantively supports a scene-securing-overlap relation.
residual_risks: Page-level inconsistency: the rendered 'Appears on' line reads 'Securing the Scene — Key — Anchor', conflicting with the frontmatter homes role 'Related (scene-securing overlap)'. Assertion tracks the frontmatter it is keyed to; the two-way discrepancy is an authoring artifact not adjudicable from disclosed evidence.

reasons: Frontmatter homes lists [[Detention and Search of Persons at the Scene]] as 'Key — Anchor', matching the assertion payload.

SCOTUS majority opinion (court_level scotus); 'Binding — SCOTUS' weight label is correct.
field_i_validity good_law (migration-seed) is correct: Summers remains good law.

Official cite 384 U.S. 436 and full parallel set (86 S. Ct. 1602; 16 L. Ed. 2d 694; 10 Ohio Misc. 9; 36 Ohio Op. 2d 237; 10 A.L.R. 3d 974) plus vendor-neutral 1966 U.S. LEXIS 2817 all match the lake citations block.
Cached opinion corroborates identity: Warren, C.J. opinion, custodial-interrogation warnings holding, star pages *440 onward, decided 1966.
Frontmatter homes and 'Appears on' both list [[Miranda and Custodial Interrogation]] as 'Key — Anchor', matching the assertion payload.
Miranda is the anchor authority for custodial-interrogation doctrine; disclosed opinion supports the anchor role.

Opinion at *444 (b542-7): 'the prosecution may not use statements... stemming from custodial interrogation... unless it demonstrates the use of procedural safeguards...', requiring warnings and a waiver 'made voluntarily, knowingly and intelligently.'
Holding field ('Statements from custodial interrogation are inadmissible unless police first gave the warnings and the suspect knowingly, voluntarily...') is an accurate paraphrase of that passage.
field_i_validity good_law (migration-seed) is correct: Miranda remains good law.
scope_note ('Reaffirmed as a constitutional rule in Dickerson v. United States') matches the content page's Treatment section and settled doctrine.
residual_risks: Cached opinion text is truncated (first ~120k of 164,991 chars); the *444 holding passage needed for these assertions is within the disclosed portion, so no reviewed assertion depends on the withheld tail.

reasons: Frontmatter homes and 'Appears on' both list [[Brady and Giglio]] as 'Key — Anchor (historical origin)', matching the assertion payload.
Mooney's knowing-use-of-perjured-testimony due-process rule (opinion *112) is the recognized historical origin of the Napue/Giglio/Brady line; anchor-historical-origin role is supported.

Opinion at *112: a conviction contrived 'through a deliberate deception of court and jury by the presentation of testimony known to be perjured' is 'as inconsistent with the rudimentary demands of justice as is the obtaining of a like result by intimidation' — supports both the due-process holding and the quoted fragment.
Disposition matches: 'leave to file the petition is denied, but without prejudice' because state habeas 'has not been invoked and it is not shown to be unavailable' (failure to exhaust).
field_i_validity good_law (migration-seed): Mooney's core due-process principle remains good law as the foundation of Napue/Giglio and the Brady disclosure line.
scope_note appropriately confines the enduring principle and flags that the procedural (exhaustion) holding reflects 1935 practice, consistent with the disclosed disposition.
residual_risks: Lake record status is 'under_review' (identity pending), but this is an identity-pipeline flag; it does not bear on the treatment/validity determination, which the disclosed opinion supports.
